verdict.reason: One blocking finding in my scope: D59 (new in this re-check, pre-existing since at least R7A-FREEZE-2, outside the FREEZE-A1 to A2 delta), a known equivalent state mode of D53. A moderate return whose pause week holds the first executed exposures of an exercise starts from a state that predates them; when that week is the athlete's first loaded week, every exercise executed before the break restarts as a first establishment: no return entry (672 of 672 exercises), the block in progress earns its set, 1,582 rows above the declared ceiling and 226 counts two sets above the largest since the return (NONE and FAMILIAR athletes, every case of the configuration). Under Founder request §10, D53 cannot be CLOSED while a known equivalent state mode allows a restoration jump, and §13 requires D53 CLOSED. Both findings of my first review are closed: D57 and D58. D56 is closed. S1 and S4-S10 hold at FREEZE-A2. The fix is runtime-only: no policy text, clinical semantics or Founder decision is needed for the ruling.

newFindings.summary: Condition 7 does not say whether a quality run eased by another adaptation, or a race touch or a race, counts as the short return's easy slot. FREEZE-A2 says no: fatigue-first gives one more easy quality session next week than return-first, and a short break in the taper or race week carries the easy slot to the first next-block threshold after the post-event week.

newFindings.owner: Product/UX with Data, then the policy revision
newFindings.summary: An easy slot not done (missed report or unreported) does not pass on, while one skipped prospectively (unavailable, event conflict) does. Next week's quality is then the held dose (41, the same as when the slot was done). Declare whether a slot made easy and not done owes its easy run.

Without the weekly review of the week holding a skipped easy slot, a report made next week does not carry it (next week keeps THRESHOLD 48, the conditional plan). Covered by the weekly-review condition of every record.

newFindings.summary: The return-cap end reads next week's count as this week's normal count plus the block set. Another rise of the normal count at a transition (the NONE-class first-block clamp, a priorSets regain) was not reached with a cap in force in 1,224 timelines (B 0); computing next week's count directly would remove the dependency.

newFindings.owner: Runtime author with Product Constitution & Governance (next policy revision)
newFindings.summary: A return ceiling set by a pre-break count fitted to a short time budget binds for many weeks once the budget rises (773 of 1,200 binding caps at the horizon are at the ceiling). Declared (strengthReturnSets, R20) and conservative; decide whether such a ceiling follows the count before the fit, still one set per whole week.

qualitySlotReadings.a_fatigueFirst: Accepted. A run eased by systemic fatigue is no longer a quality slot; the return's easy slot is the next session that would run at quality dose. Other order: the return's slot is this week's and fatigue has nothing more to ease. Both orders: no quality run after the fatigue report, every dose at or below plan; next week EASY 41 (fatigue first) or THRESHOLD 41 held (return first). Non-blocking order dependence of one session (R32).
qualitySlotReadings.b_unavailableFirst: Accepted. A skipped session is not a slot; the moved quality run is the slot if the move rule moved it, else next week's first quality slot (my E2: Tuesday skipped, next week's Tuesday EASY 41 after the review; the author's layout moves it to Thursday).
qualitySlotReadings.c_easySlotUnavailableAfter: Accepted with the weekly-review condition. It passes on at the next composition from a later week, the weekly review at the latest; until then next week shows its planned quality run (THRESHOLD 48), a plan, not an executed dose. Without that review a next-week report does not carry it (R18).
qualitySlotReadings.d_easySlotNotDone_notNamed: Accepted, non-blocking. A missed or unreported easy slot does not pass on; next week's quality is the held dose 41, equal to the control with the slot done and to a missed quality without a break (R33, G03).
qualitySlotReadings.e_noQualitySlotBeforeRace_notNamed: Accepted, non-blocking. A short break in the taper week (after its quality) or in race week keeps the race touch and the race (condition 7 reads QUALITY only, unchanged since R6) and makes the first next-block threshold after the post-event week easy (EASY 48, week 15). Conservative, one session (R32).
